newsitem.title: UK: UK toilet paper maker unveils new marketing drive.
newsitem.headline: UK toilet paper maker unveils new marketing drive.

text.p: Andrex, Britain's leading toilet paper brand, is launching a 5.7 million pound marketing campaign in a bid to compete with supermarkets' cheaper, own-brand products, U.S. owner Kimberly-Clark Corp's spokesman said on Monday.

The Andrex brand, well known in Britain for its long-running TV commercials featuring a labrador puppy tugging a seemingly endless roll of loo paper, has seen its market share fall from a third to around a quarter of the 700 million pound British market, Joe Bromilow, Kimberley-Clark's marketing manager told Reuters.
Kimberley-Clark Corp is the U.S. paper goods group which merged with Scott Paper of Canada last December. Its combined turnover amounted to some $12 billion in 1995.

"We would like to see (Andrex's) share go back to around 30 percent by volume and 35 percent by value in the long-term...it's true to say we did take our eye off the ball and lost ground to our competitors," Bromilow said.
Supermarkets' own-brand toilet rolls are reckoned to account for about half of the entire market.
Andrex's strategy is to distinguish its newly-relaunced 'softer, stronger' paper from the cheaper end of the market.

The well-established trend for supermarkets to undercut brand-leaders with own-label goods has prompted many consumer good giants -- from detergent makers to cola giants -- to fight back by emphasising the 'heritage' attached to their products.
"The lesson for any major brand is -- 'Don't get complacent, because someone will catch you up'," Bromilow said.
Andrex's advertising offensive, due to run until the end of the year and part of a 15 million pound relaunch budget, will include new television, radio and poster advertisements.
The ads are likely to call heavily on the enduring appeal of the Andrex puppy among pet-loving Britons.
"We won't be taking our foot off the gas next year either. So you can expect the marketing to continue well into 1997," the spokesman said.
However, Kimberley-Clark's expectations for improved sales must take account of only modest growth -- forecast at roughly three percent -- for the toilet paper market next year.
Kimberley-Clark, together with Scott Paper, also produces the Kleenex and Scott tissue brands.
